findings: The card-network product lets issuers and lenders provide BNPL through a customer's Mastercard Installments virtual card. A business using its Mastercard relationship is automatically enrolled when it starts accepting Mastercard payments. The qualifying card works like a regular Mastercard transaction at checkout, supports four interest-free installments and uses the regular Mastercard fee structure. Surcharging for this product is prohibited (old raw 4–12; new raw 5–13; source 13–19). Keep the merchant relationship and customer's virtual-card prerequisite distinct from approval, four merchant captures or a merchant payout schedule.

The two independent location lists contain the same seven places: customers in Australia, Canada, Germany, Malaysia, UAE, UK and US, and Stripe merchant accounts in AU, CA, DE, MY, AE, GB and US. The presentment currencies are USD, CAD, GBP, AUD, AED, MYR and EUR. No domestic-only pairing condition or all-cross-border/all-currency guarantee is stated. The properties also say customer-initiated confirmation, Cards family, standard payout timing, and yes to Connect, disputes, manual capture, and full and partial refunds (old raw 14–67; new raw 15–68). Source 21 collapses the two location axes and omits those listed product properties.

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mastercard-installments, old raw lines 4-12 and new raw lines 5-13 both describe an issuer/lender BNPL product accepted through the business's existing Mastercard relationship. Enrollment is automatic when the business starts accepting Mastercard. A customer with the Mastercard Installments virtual card pays like a regular Mastercard transaction at checkout in four interest-free installments. The regular Mastercard fee structure applies and surcharging is prohibited. In old raw lines 14-67 and new raw lines 15-68, the seven customer locations and the seven eligible Stripe business-account jurisdictions are separate lists with the same countries: Australia, Canada, Germany, Malaysia, UAE, UK and US. Presentment currencies are USD, CAD, GBP, AUD, AED, MYR and EUR. The guide labels it Cards with customer-initiated confirmation, standard payout timing, and support for Connect, disputes, manual capture and full and partial refunds. In old raw lines 68-87 and new raw lines 69-88, the extra prohibited categories are money transfer, funding transactions, quasi cash, merchandise and services: customer financial institution, payment transaction and MoneySend. Both captures label the recurring property Yes but explicitly say a recurring product or subscription attempted with this virtual card is declined. The opt-out is a Stripe Support form request with subject MC Installments Opt Out and can take 1–3 days. source-stripe-mastercard-installments.md lines 13-27 retain the core plan and recurring warning, but merge account and customer location, omit several method properties and misstate the form as email. Acceptance eligibility and customer initiation do not establish payment success or payout receipt.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mastercard-installments, old raw lines 79-81 and new raw lines 80-82 change buyer to customer while preserving the same virtual-card recurring decline. The discovery header and line shift are capture metadata, and there is no navigation or substantive behavior change. Keep the original May 1, 2026 authority dated separately from the November 7 capture. Both old raw lines 32-34 and new raw lines 33-35 still show recurring Yes, and both recurring sections explicitly describe decline. Carry the qualification reciprocally in source-stripe-mastercard-installments.md and the Mastercard section of the installments concept, which already flags it. The virtual-card restriction stays scoped to this Mastercard product. Independently, the source's email opt-out at line 27 conflicts with the form in old raw lines 83-87 and new raw lines 84-88. Preserve the exact subject, the can-take-1–3-days timing and the distinction between request and completed opt-out. In the same source, keep the customer and Stripe-account location axes distinct and describe the six named categories without implying the captures supply numeric MCCs. The card guide establishes neither a standalone BNPL API enum or redirect, nor any SetupIntent, off-session, client/server integration or version contract. The product's confirmation, capability and standard payout properties do not guarantee customer approval, successful capture or refund, a dispute outcome or funds arrival.
